title: Truth tables and De Morgan
instructions:
## Two formulas, one table

The **Truth table** tool builds the table for any formula and can compare two formulas side by side. Write *not* as `~`, *and* as `&`, *or* as `|`, *implies* as `->` and *iff* as `<->`.

## Do this

1. Fill in the truth table for `p -> q` by hand in the questions panel. Check it against the tool afterwards.
2. De Morgan's law says ¬(p ∧ q) is equivalent to something built from ¬p and ¬q. Write that formula.
3. Find a formula using only `~` and `|` that is equivalent to `p -> q`.
4. Which of these is a tautology? Enter the formula: `(p -> q) <-> (~q -> ~p)` or `(p -> q) <-> (q -> p)`. Use the tool to decide.
hints: p -> q is false only when p is true and q is false.
Push the negation inside and flip the connective: ¬(p ∧ q) ≡ ¬p ∨ ¬q.
p -> q is equivalent to ¬p ∨ q; the contrapositive ¬q -> ¬p is equivalent to the original.

realityNote: Compilers and SQL optimisers rewrite conditions with exactly these equivalences; an "if not (a and b)" in your code is a De Morgan rewrite waiting to happen.
